reason: The cited evidence (E1) only states that anti-oxidation coatings are 'still required' for HfNbTaTiZr-type alloys, which supports the general need for a coating but provides no specific evidence that a coating will successfully form a protective scale, prevent embrittlement, or preserve mechanical properties. The key mechanistic and performance premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Anti-oxidation coatings are required for high-temperature air applications of refractory high-entropy alloys
A coating can form a stable, protective Al2O3 scale that acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier
The coating will prevent oxygen-induced embrittlement without altering the bulk microstructure
The coated alloy will retain the mechanical properties (ductility, yield strength) of the untreated cast state
